task.description: Security design gate for REQ-518 (scoped data path, 404 equivalence and writes, approver rule F1). Rulings per design section 8 plus required design changes. No edits to lib/ or test/.

result.summary: DESIGN GATE: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. SCOPE: in scope (tenant-data path: 3 filter routes, 8 record write and attachment routes, 7 task routes, 3 self-service routes, tenants migration 20261019100001, secret-free). Mandatory-trigger files touched by the plan: lib/letflow/api/route_scope.ex, lib/letflow/api/scope/enforce.ex, config/test.exs (a :modules entry for fixture_scoped, if used, is a config :letflow, :modules trigger) and the snapshot file; each of 2c-i-a, 2c-i-b, 2c-ii, 2d needs its OWN SECURITY-REVIEWER code verdict quoted in the PR body with the reclassified-route table (AC 23 per PR #2801). The design is sound: predicate as outermost where plus ON clause per hop (left join keeps primary with NULL target, one-to-many collapse leaks no child count), retired nodes excluded, undeclared = false, declarations module-owned, set recomputed per request, cursor carries no set, scope lookup is one statement after an unconditional set read, scope telemetry carries closed atoms only, D8 respected (counted not audited). Seven required changes (C-1..C-7) are small design edits; none blocks 2c-i-a except C-1 and C-2 which must be in r2 before that PR is built. RULINGS: R-1 IN (conditions). R-2 class definition IN (tightened), /me/modules IN, /help/resolved IN (condition replaced), GET /me/memberships stays on 0051-A7. R-3 IN. R-4 IN (conditions; detective not preventive). R-5 IN. R-6 IN. R-7 and R-8 accepted with a compensating production-shaped test. RA-13 ACCEPTED with conditions and a requirement-text amendment before 2d merges. OQ-3 literal TASK_WORKER confirmed. See rulings object.

rulings.R-1: IN for sites 7, 8, 9 (exam session query_all, snapshot query_all, anti_cheat query_events), comment form '# scope-all: SEC-518-R1'. Basis checked: all exam routes are default-sourced :tenant_wide in test/fixtures/route_scope/tenant_wide_default_routes.txt (8 exam-sessions routes), so under on a scoped-only principal is refused 403 by Enforce before exam code runs; tenant-wide and token principals are :all by D1; exam types are undeclared so threading a scoped set would return nothing, not enforce anything. CONDITIONS: (a) the :exam_route_reclassified walk rule and the scan test (exam manifest gains scope_declarations while a literal remains) are mandatory tests in 2c-i-a/2c-i-b, and the walk rule must cover ANY route of module exam, including routes added later, not only the 8 listed; (b) list_available_exams keeps the required :scope opt (threaded, as designed); (c) the ruling lapses automatically if either guard is removed. The FALLBACK threading is therefore not needed and the build default flips to the literal form once this handoff exists.
rulings.R-2: CLASS DEFINITION 4.1: IN, with one added sentence: 'a field derived from a resource the caller must be scoped for may never be added to a :self_service response; adding one requires a new ruling and an edit of @self_service_routes'. GET /me/memberships: stays :self_service under 0051-A7 (verified: A7 in the 0051 Amendment 1 text names it as the ONE member). GET /me/modules: IN (Installs.list_installed(prefix:) is tenant-level module metadata, no caller filter, :MyModulesRead is already held by every role including CANDIDATE). GET /help/resolved: IN with a CONDITION that replaces the designer's wording: read in routers/help.ex, process_definition_id is only a FILTER over help rows and 'stale' is computed from the SELECTED HELP ROW's own process_definition_id via Definitions.get_by_id (compute_stale), never from the request id, so the route is not a definition-existence oracle. Condition: it stays so. The request id must remain a filter over help rows only; the response may carry no field read from Definitions beyond the existing boolean; a change that probes Definitions with the request id re-opens the ruling. Add a test: a process_definition_id naming an existing definition with no help row and one naming no definition give byte-identical responses for a scoped-only user. Ruling ids to record in @self_service_routes: M2 'SEC-518-R2-modules', H1 'SEC-518-R2-help'. Pre-existing, not introduced: me.ex line 96 uses a bare {:ok, memberships} = match (INV-8); advisory A-5.
rulings.R-3: IN. Production declarations cover MANAGED types only (Catalog rule 11); an unmanaged declaration is accepted only for a module id on :scope_declaration_unmanaged_modules, set in config/test.exs only and scanned by T-D8; ScopeDeclaration re-checks (defence in depth). Accepted consequence: generic record writes by scoped callers are unreachable in production (managed -> constant 403 before scope, undeclared -> 404). Conditions: (a) T-D8 must also assert that Application.get_env for the key is [] under MIX_ENV=prod config evaluation, not only a file scan; (b) config/runtime.exs must not read the key from System.get_env (scan covers it); (c) the compensating production-shaped test of R-8.
rulings.R-4: IN, as a DETECTIVE control only. Conditions: (a) docs and the PR body must say the before-send check detects a handler that omitted ScopeGate, it does not make a response safe; the preventive controls are the per-route behaviour tests T-L19..T-L26 and the ledger; the marker proves 'gate called', not 'result applied'; (b) it fires only in the on branch and only for 2xx; every non-2xx passes unchanged; (c) the replacement is the same detail-free Response.internal_error body as Enforce.fail_closed, no ids in the log; (d) the callback must itself rescue (a raise inside before_send must not leak a stack or a partial body) and answer the detail-free 500; (e) ScopeGate returns {conn, set}: a handler that drops the returned conn loses the marker and gets a false 500 under on. That is fail-closed and loud, accepted, and T-L19..26 catch it before merge; (f) the committed-write caveat of OQ-8 is accepted because the write handlers apply scope BEFORE writing (design 5.3); the only path where the 500 follows a commit is a defect that the ledger and T-B1/T-L27 must catch pre-merge; (g) export is a plain Response.ok (verified run_export in routers/entities.ex, no send_chunked), so the backstop can replace the body there; if any filter route ever streams, the backstop cannot retract and the streaming route needs its gate asserted before the first chunk.
rulings.R-5: IN. Refusal of POST create and import is Response.not_found (the same bytes as the by-id 404 and as definition_not_found for a nonexistent type, verified: render_record_command folds definition_not_found to Response.not_found). Condition: ONE answer for the batch whatever the row or reason, no count, no per-row detail; test that the type-gate refusal, an out-of-scope node, a NULL node, a retired node and a nonexistent node all give byte-identical bodies and headers (T-W5 plus C-6).
rulings.R-6: IN (conservative). A scoped caller must not write :tenant_wide masters through generic routes: that would be a privilege escalation from a scoped grant to tenant-wide data. Refusal is the generic 404 before the body is read.
rulings.R-7: ACCEPTED as corrected. A :tenant_wide declaration makes every record of the type readable by every scoped caller that passes the coarse check (T16); safety rests on module-owned declarations, managed-only production declarations and the test-only allowlist. If R-3's allowlist ever widens or OQ-4's definitions refusal is dropped, that is a precondition regression and needs a new SEC pass.
rulings.R-8: ACCEPTABLE with a compensating test. Unreachable production write paths mean AC 6-9 logic is proven only on fixture_scoped; the production-reachable safety property is that a scoped caller can write NOTHING through generic routes. Add test T-W21 (required, C-5): with the production allowlist value [] a scoped caller on every write and attachment route gets 403 entity_type_managed for a declared managed type, the generic 404 for an undeclared type and for a :tenant_wide-declared type, with no row written (database assertion). The dead-in-production write logic is otherwise accepted because it is fail-closed by default (:all default exists only for system callers, guarded by the scan).
rulings.RA-13: ACCEPTED with conditions. A principal holding the route permission TENANT-WIDE (any role, token principal, platform admin) is exempt from the TASK_WORKER grant requirement. Security basis: such a principal already has tenant-wide authority over the route permission, including :TasksAssign/:TasksReassign that move any task to any assignee, so the exemption adds no capability; D1 says tenant-wide on a permission is tenant-wide. CONDITIONS: (a) the exemption predicate is exactly Scope.allowed?(principal, route_permission, :tenant_wide) being {:allow, _} and nothing role-name based; (b) the routing-role checks stay in force for the exempt principal; (c) the mixed case (scoped TASK_WORKER plus tenant-wide PROCESS_OPERATOR) is pinned by T-F15 as exempt; (d) the requirement text of AC 13 (an 'iff') must be amended by REQ-ANALYST BEFORE PR 2d merges, and docs/roles.md must state the exemption in a paragraph separate from the three verbatim sentences of AC 17; the design may not silently diverge from an AC.
rulings.OQ-3: LITERAL TASK_WORKER grant confirmed (Scope.allowed_for_role?/3, allowed_set_for_role/2). The union reading would let a scoped PROCESS_OPERATOR grant widen the task view, contradicting 0051 D9/Q3 (PROCESS_OPERATOR rejected as approver). Do not build the wider reading without a decision-record amendment.

required_design_changes: C-1 (2c-i-a, INV-8): section 3.3 does not say what allowed_set/2 does when ScopeNodePaths.allowed_node_ids/2 returns {:error, :invalid_node_id | :invalid_schema_name}. State: it raises an internal typed error that the pipeline maps to the detail-free 500 (never :all, never a partial set, never silently :none for a config fault), one constant log line, no ids. Also define a hard cap on the expanded set (OQ-7; suggested 50,000 ids): above it, fail closed with the same 500 and a constant log line; no truncation. Test both.

C-2 (2c-i-a, test): T-C12 and T-C4 fixture tree must include a RETIRED INTERMEDIATE node with a LIVE descendant and a grant on a live ancestor of it (allowed?/3 considers only the resource node's own retired_at, scope.ex moduledoc), asserting allowed_set and allowed? agree for the descendant, and that the retired node itself is absent. Today the fixture has only retired leaf a3.

C-3 (2c-ii, INV-5): section 5.3 puts :scope_check inside the transaction AFTER the idempotency check. A scoped caller can replay an existing idempotency key with a request body naming an out-of-scope node and get the stored record (id and version) instead of the refusal. Add a pure value check (ScopedWrites) on the NEW scope value BEFORE the transaction and before the idempotency claim, for create and update, answering the same Response.not_found; keep the in-transaction check as the race backstop. Test: replay of a key created by another caller with an out-of-scope value gives the generic 404, not the stored record (new mutant MU39).

C-4 (2d, lock order): state that the :f1_scope step is a plain read (no FOR SHARE or FOR UPDATE on role_scope_grants, group, binding or org tables), runs on the transaction's own repo handle (Multi repo), after the task row lock, and reloads grants by Scope.load_grants(user_id, prefix) so group membership is fresh too; the 517 admin-plane order (A, R, G, N, B, C) and the 2704 engine order stay untouched; add a test that the existing lock-order suite is unedited and passes.
C-5 (2c-ii): add T-W21 per ruling R-8 (production-shaped config: scoped writes refused on every write and attachment route, no row written).

C-6 (2c-ii): add a bytes test that the type-gate refusal (undeclared or :tenant_wide type, scoped caller) equals the answer for a nonexistent type name on create and import, and for an unmanaged undeclared type on query the documented empty page; record in the design that type existence is not a scoped resource (definitions routes are tenant-wide only, so this is tenant-level metadata and the difference between 'undeclared existing type -> empty page' and 'nonexistent type -> RequestAccess error' on query is accepted, advisory A-2).

C-7 (process): update section 8 of the design with the ruling ids of this handoff (R-1 SEC-518-R1, R-2 ids above), remove the threading fallback as build default, add the AC 23 mapping (per-PR verdict, PR-body table of reclassified routes with method, path, old and new class, snapshot lines removed) to each PR checklist, and add config/test.exs :modules to the SECURITY-REVIEWER trigger notes for 2c-i-a.
advisories: A-1: plug lets {:resolver,_}, :filter, :self_service through after only the coarse allow (Enforce.check/3 verified), so the per-route behaviour tests, not the walk, are the control; keep T-L19..T-L26 mandatory and non-skippable.
A-2: type-name existence differs on query between a nonexistent type and an undeclared type for a scoped caller; accepted as tenant-level metadata (C-6).
A-3: idempotency-key existence across scopes is pre-existing behaviour (GH #2543 binds a key to the request, not to the actor); not changed by 518.

A-4: export runs audit_exempted after compile; with :none the exempted-fields audit still fires. Harmless, but test that a :none export returns the empty page and writes no unredacted audit for rows never returned if that is cheap.
A-5: me.ex handle_list_memberships uses a bare {:ok, memberships} = match (pre-existing INV-8 hit now reachable by scoped users); route to ELIXIR-DEV as a drive-by or an issue, not a 518 blocker.
A-6: ScopeGate must be called with the conn that is finally sent; discard of the returned conn is a false 500 under on (R-4 e).

A-7: INV-5 spot checks the code pass must repeat: attachment list for out-of-scope parent returns the same empty 200 as a nonexistent parent (EntityAttachments.list returns an empty page today, verified 1689-1704), attachment create short-circuits before the multipart read, import structural checks precede the type gate without revealing scope.

A-8: migration 20261019100001 and the Task schema field: the column must not appear in cast lists, task_json maps, or insert_all of TaskActivation; T-F2's scan should also cover insert_all and Repo.insert_all keyword forms. F1 stays fail-closed (NULL node visible only to tenant-wide).
